topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic origins and biological context of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations can produce cancer through clonal evolution when the affected cells and their environment permit it.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and their interpretation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence about environmental exposures informs the debate over whether cancer is preventable or simply a matter of bad luck.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to cancer, with Burkitt lymphoma illustrating the interaction between pathogens and cellular mutations.

topics.label: Mechanisms of DNA damage by environmental carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens damage DNA and generate mutations, sometimes through the body's own metabolic processes.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutational initiation may require a subsequent growth-promoting environment for tumours to develop.

topics.label: Tissue susceptibility and recap of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics complete and recap the account of carcinogenesis by emphasizing how biological context determines the consequences of carcinogen exposure.

topics.label: Methods for assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate how evidence linking exposures to cancer can be obtained and what the available methods can and cannot establish.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit perspective
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarizing its conclusions and framing everyday exposure decisions as balances between risks and benefits.
